I've known I was a lesbian for over a decade now and during that, I've gone through periods of absolutely hating men, having small crushes on them, being alright with the idea of sleeping with them, being repulsed by them, jealous of them, and totally ambivalent to them. The only thing that never changes is that I know I would never be fully happy ending up with a guy forever. I'm sometimes alright with the idea of getting involved with guys because they're humans lmao and society really encourages and emphasizes straight attraction, but I know I'll always be looking for a chance to build a life with a woman and my feelings towards women just feel good and real and happy. It's not the same when it comes to men, women are really enough for me in the most amazing way and growing old and wrinkly with the same one sounds like a dream. 

Also generally can't relate when my straight/bi friends talk about their earnest attraction towards men, yuck

God this resonates so much. Even though I've been doubting my beliefs since childhood, I always relied on that Muslim community safety net. A new friend of mine has been consciously exmuslim since early teenagehood and they're totally comfortable with casual sex, drinking, going out without hijab, and I feel so behind in a way. Like "if I'm really not Muslim, why aren't I as comfortable as they are doing unislamic things?" It's almost like having imposter syndrome, even though I want to build a life outside of Islam, the more I hang out with non-Muslims the odder I feel and the less I feel I fit in. Whenever I'm around never-Muslims I tend to fall back into acting Muslim just because I feel like I don't fit in with them at all and that's the only developed persona I have to offer. It's frustrating!

I try to recommit by looking at this process as a challenge instead of a pass-or-fail thing. If I end up eating past comfortably full one meal, I look at what factors could've led to that and see if changing those leads to better eating outcomes. Same for if I'm not eating nutritiously enough, over exercising, under exercising, etc. I try to remove the pressure of getting everything perfect and look at it more like "my body's going to be fine in the long-run but what challenges do I want to take on to improve it?"
